newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST-New Zealand business weeklies - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-New Zealand business weeklies - Jan 17.

text.p: A simple way to assess whether your electricity company is profiteering -- or, equally badly, making less than it should -- has been devised by a leading securities firm. Using an XY graph, ANZ Securities has charted the performances of all 40 electric power companies, using its own calculation of each company's accounting rate of profit on the vertical scale. That is the performance measure designed to test for excess monopoly profits. Page 1.

The top secret Government Communications Security Bureau (GCSB) responsible for electronic intelligence, has been accused of unnecessarily interfering with exports of encryption software for computer programmes. Encryption scrambles sensitive computer messages such as financial transactions, making them difficult to decode -- but it also has intelligence and military applications. The bureau's critics say the type of encryption software concerned is freely available on the Internet and from overseas vendors and that interference with exports is pointless. Page 1.

New Zealand's key business leaders will be able to directly question Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Treasurer Winston Peters on their plans for the economy on February 11 at an exclusive breakfast briefing in Wellington. The "Government to Business" breakfast is being hosted by The National Business Review" and co-sponsors Telecom Corporation and Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu in association with the New Zealand Employer's Federation. Page 1.

Although the way that New Zealand television will make the change to digital transmission remains uncertain, free-to-air broadcasters TVNZ and TV3 have been told that they cannot use UHF frequencies reserved for public use during the transition period during which could last more than a decade. TVNZ and TV3 broadcast an analogue signal which occupies all the very high frequency (VHF) spectrum available nationally for television. Page 3.

In a submission to the US National Trade Estimate Report on Foreign Trade Barriers, the Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America group (PHRMA) has lashed a Pharmac policy that effectively restricts entry to the New Zealand market. The submission has been strongly endorsed by Kim Miles, the chief executive of PHRMA's New Zealand equivalent, the Researched Medicines Industry (RMI). "We believe this to be an extremely good summation of the New Zealand situation," Miles said. Page 7.

The quality of figures in the government's accounts are open to question, a US report has found. A paper issued by the New York-based International Federation of Accountants, written by two New Zealand experts, notes some figures in the accounts are not covered by generally accepted accounting practice (GAAP). This is because there are no standards for issues specific to governments such as measuring infrastructure, heritage and defence assets, tax revenues and welfare obligations. Page 13.
